html:
The journey of the Chinese Buddhist monk Xuanzang to India, which began in 629 and ended with his return to Chang'an in 645. He wanted the original Sanskrit texts to settle questions about Buddhist teaching.

He left without the emperor's permission and went by land: across the desert, through the oasis towns of Central Asia, over the Hindu Kush past the great Buddhas of Bamiyan, and down into the plains of India. He spent years at Nalanda, the great Buddhist monastery and centre of learning, and visited the places of the Buddha's life. King Harsha honoured him at a great assembly at Kannauj.

He came home with more than 650 texts and spent the rest of his life translating them. His account, the Great Tang Records on the Western Regions, written for Emperor Taizong, is one of the best sources for India and Central Asia in the 600s. The journey later grew into the novel Journey to the West.
